Official basis, per vehicle per year.
What the vehicle selects, and what it does not. Clicking a truck selects the catalogue - the part families that belong in that zone. It is not a per-model parts split, and this page will not pretend otherwise. The billing behind every number is keyed on the distributor and the part number; it carries no model code, so nobody can say from this data how much of a brake disc sat on an N-Series rather than a D-Max. The model cut becomes possible when the EPC attribution pull is run, and until then the series table below shows fleet and the official target, clearly labelled as context rather than as a parts split.
Limits, stated plainly.
  • The six zones cover € of the €34,993,609 billed. The remaining €2,894,944 sits in the two placeholder buckets, Other / review and UNCLASSIFIED, which are not physical and are named here rather than forced onto a truck.
  • Five zones are positional: the family really does live there. The sixth, electrical, is functional - a sensor or a loom runs the length of a vehicle, so it is grouped by what it does, not by where it sits.
  • The percentage is a base-price move on the quantity-weighted prior base price. It is not a revenue, margin or elasticity outcome, and no demand response is modelled.
  • The AIM tree classifies 164,667 part numbers; 15,872 of them billed in this window and 15,812 of those sit in the tree. The zone totals describe the billing, not the catalogue depth.
  • Israel is UMI and UTI separately, never blended.
